title: Circuit-aware tapered routing and tenant safety lanes for staged model rollouts
creator: Miguel Torres
description:
Goal: introduce a circuit-aware tapered routing layer that orchestrates per-tenant safety lanes during staged model rollouts. This ticket implements a lightweight Router augmentation that annotates requests with circuit state and tenant-lane metadata, a taper controller which applies exponential weight schedules for canaries, and failover semantics that prioritize preserving KV caches for in-flight sessions across regional or capacity-tier spillovers.

Scope: router annotation + lookup cache, taper controller service, rollout config schema changes, small runtime changes to preserve KV caches on standby nodes, observability (dashboard and alerts), end-to-end tests and a staged rollout plan. Out of scope: full pricing-tier hedging, RBAC UI for lane creation (follow-up PM ticket).

Success criteria: smooth canary ramping with reduced oscillation under load, automatic soft-failover to standby region without cache loss for active sessions, clear rollback triggers (latency P95 and token-cost increase), and no SLO regression for non-canary tenants during rollouts.
comments: 2025-02-12: Spike complete. Implemented prototype gate in routing layer that tags flows with circuit state and tenant lane. Observed ~12% extra lookup latency in synthetic tests — may need optimization in route lookup cache.

2025-02-13: Design review with PM/Infra. Emma Li: prefer an exponentially-weighted taper rather than linear ramp for tenant safety lanes to reduce oscillation under backpressure. Action: update canary schedule to allow configurable decay factor.

2025-02-14: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3124 — implements circuit-state annotation and per-tenant taper controller. Needs perf benchmarks and unit tests; flagged to SRE for staging load testing.

2025-02-15: Staging load test (us-west-2 + eu-west-1) with mixed variants: results show KV cache preservation is necessary for soft failover — failing over without warming increases token cost ~3x for affected sessions. Added plan to implement 'soft-warm' KV preservation policy on standby nodes.
2025-02-16: Security review scheduled 2025-02-20. Compliance asked to include audit logs for lane promotions and spillbacks. Added audit hook to rollout API and updated design doc.
2025-02-17: QA found a race when tenant lane changes mid-request leading to duplicate downstream calls. Mitigation: add atomic route-ownership transfer backed by Router v2 sticky leases.

2025-02-18: Rebased PR; requesting review from runtime-owners and SRE. Next: perf micro-optimizations, add canary observability dashboard (console rollouts panel) and implement auto-rollback signatures tied to P95 latency and token-cost delta thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: Router annotates requests with circuit-state and tenant-lane tags (unit tests pass)
Canary tapering strategy exposes per-tenant weight schedule and can be overridden via rollout config
Automatic spillback to regional standby when lane enters degraded state without losing KV cache for active sessions
Dashboard shows per-tenant canary metrics (latency P50/P95, token cost, error rate) and highlights auto-rollback triggers
End-to-end test validates canary taper and rollback within 15 minutes under synthetic error injection
notes: Tradeoff: preserving KV caches across failover increases memory footprint on standby nodes — may require a soft-warm policy to limit eviction and cap memory used per-tenant.
If routing lookup extra latency remains >5ms we will move circuit annotations into a lightweight header emitted by the edge gateway to avoid hotpath regression in Router.
Consider future extension: combine tenant-priority hedging and pricing tier signals to dynamically shrink blast radius for low-value tenants during risky rollouts.
